newsitem.title: UKRAINE: World Bank suspends $317 mln Ukraine energy loan.
newsitem.headline: World Bank suspends $317 mln Ukraine energy loan.

text.p: The World Bank said on Thursday it had suspended a $317 million loan to Ukraine to develop its electricity market after the former Soviet republic delayed charging consumers 100 percent of the cost of electricity.
"The suspension was triggered by the indefinite postponement of a previously agreed increase of electricity prices," a World Bank statement said.
"This delay has jeopardised the financial viability of the thermal generation companies, the recipients of disbursements under this loan," it said.
The statement added funding would resume once Ukraine, now charging consumers 80 percent of power costs, raised its rates.

At the weekend Serhiy Tyhypko, deputy prime minister overseeing economic reform strategy, said Ukraine had told the International Monetary Fund it would not raise rates to 100 percent, although the IMF had repeatedly asked it to do so.
Ukraine regularly shuts down power to state-owned businesses which are not paying their bills but has put off rate increases.
The World Bank issued the loan to help Ukraine develop a wholesale electricity market, which provided working capital to generating companies established for the market.
"The operation of the market...has been hampered by the government's maintaining retail electricity prices at artificially low levels and inadequate payment collections," the statement said.
Roman Shpek, head of the National Agency of Ukraine for Reconstruction and Development, said newly-appointed Energy Minister Olexiy Sheberstov would meet World Bank representatives on Friday.
"The Ukrainian side must fulfil its responsibilities," Shpek told a news conference, adding that as of July 14 it had only fulfilled three of 10 conditions to receive the credit.
"Everything will be done to prevent credit from being stopped," Shpek said.
